subject: Hosted volume ladder and overshoot terms — clarifying minimum guarantee and burst pricing
messages:
From: Alex Patel <alex@helios.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@helios.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted usage question — commitments + overshoot

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We loved Redwood's latency numbers. Procurement asked me to follow up with a couple of clarifying questions around the hosted billing model before we put together a formal request: 

1) Minimum guaranteed spend: if we commit to a monthly floor, what happens to unused commit? Is there a 12-month true-up or can unused commit roll forward?
2) Overshoot/overspend: if our production traffic briefly exceeds the commit (burst), what on-demand rate would apply? Is there a different "overshoot" rate vs standard on-demand?
3) Volume ladder: do you provide step discounts (e.g., 0-1B tokens, 1B-5B tokens, 5B+ tokens) for hosted per-token pricing? How aggressive are cuts for higher bands?

I attached our Q4 projected consumption for context. Would appreciate a short note we can share with procurement.

Best,
Alex
Head of Cloud Ops
Helios AI

Attachment: Helios_Q4_requirements.pdf (PDF, 120KB)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Alex Patel <alex@helios.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted usage question — commitments + overshoot

Alex — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Aditya for pricing detail and Lauren for legal/contract nuance. Quick answers up front and then Aditya will drop the banded table: 

- Unused commit: we offer two options: 12-month true-up (unused commit can be credited back on a rolling basis across the 12-month term) or a roll-forward credit for up to three billing cycles if you choose an annual prepay. We can outline both in the SOW.
- Overshoot / burst: short bursts are billed at an "overshoot" rate which is typically 1.6x the committed per-token rate for that band (rather than the standard on-demand list price). That rate is designed to be materially cheaper than straight on-demand while preserving fairness across customers.
- Volume ladder: yes — we publish tiered bands. Example bands are: 0-500M, 500M-2B, 2B-10B, 10B+. The delta between adjacent bands ranges from ~10%-30% depending on model family (higher for large-context LLMs).

Aditya — can you attach a sample hosted-pricing spreadsheet with specific per-token numbers for Helios's projected mix? Lauren — any contract caveats on the roll-forward vs true-up options?

Thanks,
Priya
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Cell: +1 415-555-0198

Attachment: redwood-hosted-commit-v1.xlsx (XLSX, 24KB)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Alex Patel <alex@helios.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 14:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted usage question — commitments + overshoot

Alex / team — attaching the sample banded pricing for the projected mix you shared. A few notes: 

- The spreadsheet assumes a mixed workload (70% text-gen, 30% embedding + rerank). Per-token here means input+output tokens aggregated.
- Band example (per-token cents):
  • 0–500M: $0.0009 / token
  • 500M–2B: $0.00072 / token (20% discount)
  • 2B–10B: $0.00057 / token (21% discount)
  • 10B+: custom-negotiated, typically 30–45% off list depending on commit length and model family.

- Overshoot behavior: if you exceed the committed band in a month but stay within the next band, overshoot units are billed at the overshoot multiplier (1.6x) of the lower-band committed rate until we reconcile at month-end. If monthly usage ends up permanently higher, the true-up reconciles to the ladder on a monthly lookback over the quarter.

- Minimum guarantee scenarios:
  1) Monthly minimum (refund via credits) + 12-month true-up: unused commit is credited and netted before year-end true-up.
  2) Annual prepay: unused commit can roll-forward up to three billing months, but only if you keep the annual contract — otherwise credits are issued.

I've left comment cells in the sheet for Helios-specific blends. Happy to run a short model with your expected token mix and give a blended per-token escalator.

—Aditya
Head of Pricing, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-hosted-commit-v1.xlsx (revised)

From: Alex Patel <alex@helios.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@helios.ai
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 08:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted usage question — commitments + overshoot

Thanks — that helps a lot. A couple of follow-ups from procurement after reviewing the sheet: 

1) Overshoot multiplier: procurement would prefer the overshoot multiplier be capped for the first three months of production at 1.3x instead of 1.6x (they expect an initial ramp where bursts are common). Can you do that for a first-year ramp?
2) Minimum guarantee: they want the unused commit to roll forward for 6 months (not 3) when we do an annual prepay — is that something Redwood would accept as a concession for a 12-month committed spend?
3) Band elasticity: Helios is asking if the 10B+ band could have a floor price (i.e., a guaranteed max per-token) in the contract so we have predictability when we scale aggressive models in Q2.

Would love a concise written response we can use in our procurement memo. If we can land on the first-year ramp concession and 6-month roll-forward, procurement will push the draft SOW to legal.

Best,
Alex

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Alex Patel <alex@helios.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted usage question — commitments + overshoot

Alex — thanks for the specific asks. Walking through each point and proposing firm language we can include in the SOW/SLA: 

1) Overshoot multiplier ramp cap: Redwood can commit to a capped overshoot multiplier of 1.3x for the first three billing months after production go-live for usage that exceeds committed bands. After month three, the standard overshoot multiplier of 1.6x applies unless otherwise agreed in writing. If Helios prefers a six-month ramp cap, we can consider it tied to a higher minimum commit or a blended prepay.

Suggested clause (short):
"For the first three (3) billing months following production go-live, overshoot units will be charged at a maximum of 1.3x the committed per-token rate for the applicable band. Thereafter, overshoot units will be charged at the standard overshoot multiplier of 1.6x unless an alternative arrangement is mutually agreed in writing."

2) Roll-forward on annual prepay: Redwood can extend roll-forward credits up to three (3) billing months by default. We can offer a one-time concession to six (6) months provided Helios signs a 12-month annual prepay at or above the agreed minimum commit level of $350k/month equivalent. Proposed language:
"If Customer executes an annual prepayment equal to or greater than $4.2M for the term, the Provider will allow unused committed units to roll forward for up to six (6) consecutive billing months. Roll-forward credits expire at the end of the six-month period and are not transferable."

3) 10B+ band floor price / cap: Redwood can agree to a contracted maximum per-token list price for the 10B+ tier to give predictability. The concrete number needs negotiation — common approach is to set a floor cap tied to model family and term length with a CPI or cost-based escalator. If Helios shares a 12-month forecast for Q2 model mix, we will propose a not-to-exceed per-token ceiling for that band.

Next steps: 
- Aditya will run a blended model with Helios's Q2 forecast to propose a 10B+ not-to-exceed price.
- If Helios confirms willingness to commit to the $4.2M annual prepay threshold, we will include the six-month roll-forward clause.
- Legal will draft the simple overshoot-ramp language above for the SOW.

I can put a one-page memo for procurement summarizing the points if that helps. Happy to jump on a 20-min call tomorrow morning to finalize.

Thanks,
Priya
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Priya.Natarajan@redwood.com
